title: Ordinary module direct image commutes with open restriction
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g:T\prime\to T$ and $g\prime:X\prime\to X$ be open immersions, and let $f\prime:X\prime\to T\prime$ make the square cartesian. On categories of sheaves of structure-sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction along $g$ after ordinary direct image along $f$ is naturally isomorphic to ordinary direct image along $f\prime$ after restriction along $g\prime$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. No finiteness or quasi-coherence hypotheses are imposed.

source.place: pushforwardRestrictHom, isIso_pushforwardRestrictHom_app_app, and pushforwardRestrictIso, lines 56-96; the underived comparison used in Stacks Tag 02O5 property (a).

proof.text: Use the restriction/direct-image adjunction unit on X and its counit on T, together with functoriality of direct image for the commutative square, to define pushforwardRestrictHom. These are natural transformations, hence their whiskerings and composite are natural in the module.

For an open V of Tprime, the component is, up to the canonical restriction identifications, the restriction from f inverse-image g(V) to gprime(gprime inverse-image(f inverse-image g(V))). The cartesian square and the fact that gprime is an open immersion imply f inverse-image g(V) = gprime(fprime inverse-image V), so the two opens coincide. Every component is therefore invertible; the forgetful functor to presheaves reflects isomorphisms. Apply asIso to the natural transformation. This is precisely the existing, fully proved pushforwardRestrictIso, and applies also to empty opens.
